At the time the Cai general Dong Chongzhi had been demoted to Registrar of Chun Prefecture. Su memorialized asking that Chongzhi be pardoned and granted to him, fit for service at the front. An edict at once recalled him and sent him to the Wuning Army, and Su appointed him a guard officer. Su defeated the bandits at Jinxiang in eleven battles, captured fifty bandit generals, and killed or captured more than ten thousand. When Ziqing was pacified there were plans for action in Yan and Zhao. In the ninth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe Su was made Acting Left Vice Director, Co-Equal with the Secretariat, Chief Ministerial Prefect of Lu Prefecture, and military governor of Zhaoyi, and was granted a residence in Xingning Ward. In the tenth month Wang Chengzong died. Tian Hongzheng of Weibo was transferred to Zhen Prefecture. When Su reached Lu Prefecture, in the fourth month he was moved to Chief Ministerial Prefect of Wei Prefecture and military governor of Weibo. In the first year of Changqing You and Zhen rebelled again. When Su heard it he put on plain clothes and ordered the whole army, saying, "The reason the people of Wei are rich and can receive the sage's transforming influence is because of Lord Tian. The Son of Heaven, because he is humane and loves men, sent him to govern Zhen and Ji. Moreover Lord Tian came from Wei and led the army seven years. In one morning the men of Zhen were wicked and dared such slaughter, as though Wei had no men. If fathers, elder brothers, sons, and younger brothers who ate Lord Tian's grace—how can they repay it?" The crowd all wept bitterly. He also gave Niu Yuanji a jade belt and precious sword and sent a messenger saying to him, "My forebear once established great merit with this sword. I too pacified the Cai bandits with it. Now the men of Zhen rebel. Use this to cut them down." Yuanji received the order with gratitude and had the sword and belt displayed in the army, replying, "I wish to follow with my force and spend my life to the end." Just as arrangements were being made illness seized him. He could not govern the army. Men broke discipline, and the enterprise came to nothing. The court replaced him with Tian Bu, made him Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and sent him back to the eastern capital. That year in the tenth month he died in Luoyang at the age of forty-nine. Muzong heard and was shaken with grief. Funeral gifts were raised a grade and he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
33
始，晟克復京城，市不改肆； 及愬平淮蔡，復踵其美。 父子仍建大勛，雖昆仲皆領兵符，而功業不侔於愬，近代無以比倫。 加以行己有常，儉不違禮，弟兄席父勛寵，率以仆馬第宅相矜，唯愬六遷大鎮，所處先人舊宅一院而已。 晚歲忽於取士，辟請不得其人，至使吏緣為奸，軍政不肅，物論稍減，惜哉！
At first, when Sheng recovered the capital, the markets did not change their stalls; when Su pacified Huai and Cai he followed in that excellence. Father and son both built great merit. Though the brothers all held military seals, none matched Su in achievement. In recent times there has been no comparison. Moreover, his conduct was steady and his frugality never breached propriety. His brothers, resting on their father's honors, mostly vied in servants, horses, and grand houses; only Su, across six promotions to major commands, kept no more than a single courtyard of the family's old home. In his later years he grew careless about recruiting talent, and the men he summoned were not the right ones. Clerks turned the openings to corruption, military discipline slackened, and his reputation suffered — a pity.
34
聽七歲以廕授太常寺協律郎，常入公署，吏胥小之，不為致敬，聽令鞭之見血，父晟奇之。 後隨吐突承璀討王承宗，為神策行營兵馬使。 時昭義盧從史持兩端，無心討賊，承璀用聽計，擒從史以獻。 轉左驍衛將軍、兼御史中丞。 出為安州刺史，隨鄂嶽觀察使柳公綽討吳元濟，軍中動靜，悉用聽謀，軍聲遂振。 元和中，討李師道，聽為楚州刺史，統淮南之師。 鄆人素易淮軍，聽潛訓練，出其不意，趨海州，據險要，破沐陽兵，降朐山戍，懷仁、東海兩城望風乞降，山東平。 元和十四年五月，以功授檢校左散騎常侍、夏州刺史、夏綏銀宥節度使。 十五年六月，改靈州大都督府長史、靈鹽節度使。 境內有光祿渠，廢塞歲久，欲起屯田以代轉輸，聽復開決舊渠，溉田千余頃，至今賴之。 就加檢校工部尚書。
At seven, Ting received the hereditary post of Coordinating Music Master in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. He often came to the government offices; petty clerks slighted him and would not bow. Ting had them whipped until the blood ran. His father Sheng was astonished. He later followed Tutu Chenghui against Wang Chengzong as Military Horse Commissioner of the Divine Strategy campaign headquarters. Lu Congshi of Zhaoyi was hedging and had no will to fight the rebels. Chenghui adopted Ting's plan, seized Congshi, and presented him to the court. He was transferred to General of the Left Majestic Guard with concurrent appointment as Censor-in-Chief. Sent out as Prefect of An Prefecture, he joined Observation Commissioner Liu Gongchuo of E-Yue against Wu Yuanji. Every movement in the army followed Ting's counsel, and the army's reputation soared. During the Yuanhe era campaign against Li Shidao, Ting served as Prefect of Chu Prefecture, commanding the Huainan army. The men of Yan had long despised the Huainan troops. Ting drilled his men in secret, struck by surprise, raced to Haizhou, seized the key positions, routed the Muyang garrison, took Qushan, and Huairen and Donghai surrendered at the news — Shandong was pacified. In the fifth month of Yuanhe 14, he was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant, Prefect of Xia Prefecture, and Military Governor of Xia-Sui-Yin-You for his achievements. In the sixth month of the following year, he was reassigned as Chief Administrator of Ling Prefecture and Military Governor of Ling-Yan. The Guanglu Canal within his territory had been blocked for years. Seeking to replace grain transport with military colonies, Ting reopened the old channel and irrigated more than a thousand qing of land — the region still depends on it. He was thereupon additionally appointed Acting Minister of Works.
35
初，聽為羽林將軍，有名馬，穆宗在東宮，令近侍諷聽獻之，聽以職總親軍，不敢從。 及即位之始，幽、冀不廷，太原與二鎮接境，方議易帥，宰臣進擬，上皆不允，謂宰臣曰：「李聽為羽林將軍，不與朕馬，是必可任。」 長慶二年二月，授檢校兵部尚書、太原尹、北京留守、河東節度使，代裴度。 四年七月，轉滑州刺史、義成軍節度使。 大和二年，討李同捷。 時魏博行營將丌誌沼潛結滄、鎮，擅回戈攻其帥史憲誠。 詔聽帥師援之，大破其叛卒，誌沼奔鎮州，為王庭湊所殺，聽遂凱旋，以功封涼國公，授一子五品官。 王庭湊再違朝旨，詔聽以全師屯貝州。 路由魏州，史憲誠懼聽見襲，衷甲郊迎，候吏密白呼，乃令兵士匣刃櫜弓，休於野外，魏人遂安。 後憲誠欲入覲，竭其府庫，魏人怨之，殺憲誠，衙軍立其大將何進滔。 詔聽兼領魏博節度使，將兵北渡，魏人不納聽，乘城拒守，乃屯兵館陶。 魏兵遽襲，聽不為備，其軍大敗，無復部伍，晝夜奔走，僅而獲免，喪師過半，輜車兵仗並皆委棄。 御史中丞溫造、殿中侍御史崔蠡彈之曰：
When Ting was General of the Feathered Forest Guard, he owned a celebrated horse. Muzong, still heir apparent, had attendants suggest that Ting offer it up. Ting, commanding the imperial guard, refused. Early in his reign, You and Ji defied the court. Taiyuan bordered both regions, and the court was choosing a new commander. The chief ministers proposed candidates, but the emperor rejected them all. He told his ministers, "Li Ting would not give me his horse when he was Feathered Forest general — that man can be trusted." In the second month of Changqing 2, he was made Acting Minister of War, Magistrate of Taiyuan, Defender of the Northern Capital, and Hedong Military Governor, replacing Pei Du. In the seventh month of the fourth year, he was transferred to Prefect of Hua Prefecture and Military Governor of the Yicheng Army. In Dahe 2, he campaigned against Li Tongjie. The Weibo campaign general Qi Zhizhao secretly aligned with Cang and Zhen, turned his troops without orders, and attacked his own commander Shi Xianjing. An edict ordered Ting to march to his relief. He crushed the mutineers. Zhizhao fled to Zhen Prefecture and was killed by Wang Tingcou. Ting returned in triumph, was enfeoffed Duke of Liang, and one son received a fifth-rank post. When Wang Tingcou again defied the court, an edict ordered Ting to camp his full army at Bei Prefecture. Passing through Wei Prefecture, Shi Xianjing feared an attack and met him outside the walls in hidden armor. A clerk secretly warned Ting, who ordered his men to sheath swords, case bows, and camp in the open — the people of Wei were reassured. Later Xianjing prepared to go to court and drained the treasury. The people of Wei, resentful, killed him; the garrison installed his grand general He Jintao. Ting was ordered to take the Weibo command as well. He led troops north across the river, but Wei would not admit him; they manned the walls, and he encamped at Guantao. Wei troops struck without warning. Unprepared, Ting's army was shattered and lost all order. They fled day and night, barely escaping alive. More than half the force was lost, with wagons and arms abandoned. Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao and Palace Attendant Censor Cui Li impeached him:
36
「臣聞賞罰不立，無以示天下； 是非一貫，莫能建大中。 竊見義成軍節度使李聽，昨者資其承藉，委以統戎，俾代憲誠，付之雄鎮。 總二萬虎貔之旅，位極寵榮； 兼兩籓節制之權，心無報效。 況陛下授以神算，假以天威，入魏之期，克日先定。 而聽擁旄觀望，按甲遷延，熒惑人心，逗撓軍政。 遂使憲誠陷於屠戮，亂眾肆其奸兇，失六郡於垂成，固危巢於已覆。 委貝州而不守，燒劫無遺； 望淺口而疾驅，狼狽就道。 自圖茍免，不吝苞羞，蔑棄朝章，有同兒戲。 魏州之亂，職聽之由，論其負恩，萬死猶幸。 伏以封常清河南失律，斬於關門； 高霞寓唐鄧破傷，投諸遐裔； 渾鎬節制易定，將戰而兵力不支； 袁滋逗留西川，欲進而兇渠尚在。 或親當矢石，或躬歷艱危，勢屈賊鋒，竟申朝典，未曾貸法，必震皇威。 今李聽罪狀夙聞，中外憤惋，比之常清等輩，萬萬過之。 若陛下猶示含弘，不置極法，臣等恐憲章墜地，天下寒心。 伏請付法。」
"We have heard that when reward and punishment are not fixed, there is no way to govern the realm; when right and wrong are not applied consistently, the great order cannot be upheld. We observe that Li Ting of the Yicheng Army, relying on family standing, was entrusted with troops, set to replace Xianjing, and given a great command. He commanded twenty thousand crack troops and stood at the summit of imperial favor; he held two circuits' authority, yet his heart showed no repayment. Your Majesty gave him divine strategy and lent him imperial authority; the day of entering Wei was set in advance. Yet Ting, banner in hand, looked on and waited, holding his armor in delay, sowing confusion and frustrating the campaign. Thus Xianjing was slaughtered, rebels ran wild, six prefectures were lost on the verge of success, and a new danger was entrenched where the old had already fallen. He abandoned Bei Prefecture undefended, leaving nothing unburned or unplundered; he looked toward Qian Pass and fled headlong, leaving in disarray. seeking only to save himself, he spared no shame and treated court law as child's play. Wei's turmoil arose from Ting's conduct; for such betrayal of favor, even death ten thousand times would be mercy. We submit: Feng Changqing, for losing discipline in Henan, was beheaded at the pass; Gao Xiayu, defeated at Tang and Deng, was banished to the frontier; Hun Gao, commanding Yi and Ding, was about to fight when his strength failed; Yuan Zi lingered in Xichuan, wishing to advance while the rebel chief still lived. Some faced arrows in person, others braved peril themselves; though beaten by the enemy, the court's law was enforced. The law was never waived — imperial majesty was upheld. Li Ting's crimes have long been known; court and country alike are outraged. Compared with Feng Changqing and his like, he exceeds them ten thousandfold. If Your Majesty still shows mercy and withholds the severest penalty, we fear the law will collapse and the realm will lose heart. We respectfully ask that he be handed over to the law."
37
上不之罪，罷兵柄，為太子少師。
The emperor did not punish him. He was stripped of military command and made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
38
聽頗賂遺權幸以為援，居無何，復檢校司徒，起為邠寧節度使。 邠州衙廳，相傳不利葺修，以至隳環，聽曰：「帥臣鑿兇門而出，豈有拘於巫祝而隳公署耶！」 遂命葺之，卒無變異。 大和六年，轉武寧軍節度使。 時聽有蒼頭為徐州將，不欲聽至，聽先使親吏慰勞徐人，為蒼頭所殺。 聽不敢進，固以疾辭，用為太子太保。 七年，出守鳳翔，時人榮之。 九年，改陳許節度，未至鎮，復除太子太保分司。 開成元年，出為河中尹、河中晉慈隰節度使。 四年，以疾求代，除太子太保。 是歲十月卒，時年六十一，贈司徒。
Ting lavished gifts on powerful favorites for support. Before long he was again made Acting Grand Master of the Palace and recalled as Military Governor of Bin-Ning. Bin Prefecture's commandery hall was said to bring ill luck if repaired, and had fallen to ruin. Ting said, "A commander breaks through the Gate of Ill Omen to march forth — how can he be bound by shamans and let public offices crumble!" He ordered it repaired, and nothing untoward occurred. In Dahe 6, he was transferred to Military Governor of the Wuning Army. A household slave of Ting's served as a Xuzhou commander and did not want him to come. Ting first sent a trusted clerk to console the people of Xu, but the slave had him killed. Ting dared not advance and firmly resigned on grounds of illness; he was made Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent. In the seventh year he went out to guard Fengxiang — an appointment people of the time regarded as an honor. In the ninth year he was reassigned to the Chen-Xu command, but before reaching his post was again made Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent in nominal service. In Kaicheng 1, he went out as Magistrate of Hezhong and Military Governor of Hezhong-Jin-Ci-Li. In the fourth year he asked to be relieved on grounds of illness and was appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent. He died that tenth month at sixty-one and was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace.
39
聽十領節旌，所不至者三鎮。 蒞官苛細，好將迎遺賂，故急於聚斂，窮極侈欲。 位至一品，竟終牖下，非西平之遺德，焉能及此乎！
Ting held military governorship ten times; only three commands he never reached. In office he was exacting and severe, fond of grand welcomes and gifts, and therefore eager to amass wealth to the limit of extravagance. He rose to the first rank yet died at home in peace — without the Western Pacifier's legacy, how could he have risen so high!
40
憲，晟第五子。 晟十子，憲、愬最仁孝。 及長，好儒術，以禮法修整，起家太原府參軍、醴泉縣尉。 於頔鎮襄陽，辟為從事。 時吳少誠據淮西，獨憚頔之威，當時鹹以憲謀畫致之。 元和八年，田弘正以魏博奉朝旨，辟憲為從事，授衛州刺史，遷絳州，所至以理行稱。 入為宗正少卿，遷光祿卿。 穆宗即位，以太和公主降回鶻，命金吾大將軍胡證充送公主使，命憲副之。 使還，獻《入蕃道里記》，遷檢校左散騎常侍，兼太府卿。 出為洪州刺史、江西觀察使。 大行二年，轉嶺南節度使。 憲雖勛伐之家，然累歷事任，皆以吏能擢用，所履官秩，政績流聞。 性本明恕，尤精律學，屢詳決冤獄，活無罪者數百人。 以能入官，官無敗事，士君子多之。 大和三年八月卒，時年五十六。
Xian was Sheng's fifth son. Of Sheng's ten sons, Xian and Su were the most benevolent and filial. When grown, he loved Confucian learning and conducted himself by rites and law. He began as Registrar of Taiyuan Prefecture and Magistrate of Liquan County. When Yu Di governed Xiangyang, he recruited Xian as an aide. Wu Shaocheng then held Huaxi and feared only Yu Di's might — contemporaries credited Xian's counsel. In Yuanhe 8, Tian Hongzheng of Weibo submitted to the court and recruited Xian, appointing him Prefect of Wei Prefecture and then transferring him to Jiang; everywhere he served he was praised for good governance. He entered court as Junior Director of the Imperial Clan and was promoted to Director of Imperial Entertainments. When Muzong took the throne, Princess Taihe was sent to marry the Uyghurs. Grand General Hu Zheng of the Golden Guard was made chief escort envoy, with Xian as deputy. On his return he presented the Record of Routes into the Barbarian Lands and was promoted to Acting Left Regular Attendant with concurrent appointment as Director of the Treasury. He went out as Prefect of Hong Prefecture and Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi. In Dahe 2, he was transferred to Military Governor of Lingnan. Though from a family of martial achievement, Xian rose through repeated offices on administrative merit; his governance was widely praised at every post. Clear-minded and forgiving by nature, he was especially skilled in penal law. He repeatedly reviewed wrongful cases and saved hundreds of innocent men. Promoted for ability, he left no post in failure — gentlemen widely approved of him. He died in the eighth month of Dahe 3 at fifty-six.
41
憑累歷諸衛大將軍，恕太子洗馬，並以廕授官，累遷至少卿監。
Ping rose through grand generalships of various guards; Shu served as Groom of the Heir Apparent's Stud — both entered by hereditary privilege and rose to junior director and directorate posts.
42
惎累官至右龍武大將軍，沈湎酒色，恣為豪侈，積債至數千萬。 其子貸回鶻錢一萬余貫不償，為回鶻所訴，文宗怒，貶惎為定州司法參軍。
Ji rose to Grand General of the Right Dragon Martial Guard. He drowned in wine and women, lived in reckless luxury, and ran up debts of tens of millions. His son borrowed more than ten thousand strings of Uyghur cash and failed to repay. The Uyghurs sued; Wenzong was enraged and demoted Ji to Legal Adjutant of Ding Prefecture.
43
王佖，晟之甥。 雄武善騎射，自晟河西、河北出師，佖無役不從。 硃泚之亂，晟攻賊於光泰門，賊鋒尚勁，佖與兵馬使李演逾苑墻血戰，敗賊前鋒，諸軍方振，論功為神策將。 吐蕃之寇涇原，佖伏卒擊尚結贊，幾獲，由是深為吐蕃所畏。 晟視佖恩寵與願、愬不殊，給與過之。 晟既為張延賞媒孽罷兵權，亦不用佖為將帥，入為左衛上將軍。 元和中，願、愬醖兄弟在方鎮，佖檢校工部尚書、靈州大都督府長史、朔方靈鹽節度使。 先是，吐蕃欲成烏蘭橋於河壖，先貯材木，朔方節度使每遣人潛載之，委於河流，終莫能成。 至是，蕃人知佖貪而無謀，先厚遺之，然後併役成橋，仍築月城圍守之。 自是朔方禦寇不暇，邊上至今為恨。 長慶三年四月卒。
Wang Bi was Sheng's nephew. Bold and skilled in riding and archery, Bi followed Sheng on every campaign west and north of the river. In Zhu Ci's rebellion, Sheng attacked at Guangtai Gate while the rebel line was still strong. Bi and Military Horse Commissioner Li Yan scaled the park wall and fought through blood, routing the vanguard. The armies rallied; for merit Bi was made a Divine Strategy general. When the Tibetans raided Jingyuan, Bi ambushed and struck Shang Jiezan, nearly capturing him — from then on the Tibetans deeply feared him. Sheng favored Bi no less than Yuan and Su, and gave him even more. After Zhang Yanshang's slander cost Sheng his command, he also ceased employing Bi as a general; Bi entered court as Senior General of the Left Guard. In the Yuanhe era, while Yuan and Su held regional commands, Bi was made Acting Minister of Works, Chief Administrator of Ling Prefecture, and Shofang-Ling-Yan Military Governor. The Tibetans had long sought to build the Wulan Bridge on the riverbank and stockpiled timber. Each Shofang governor secretly sent men to dump the materials into the river, and the bridge was never finished. The Tibetans, knowing Bi greedy and unwise, bribed him heavily, then finished the bridge and built a crescent fortress to hold it. From then on Shofang could not keep pace with frontier defense, and the border still bears the grudge. He died in the fourth month of Changqing 3.
44
史臣曰：西平器偉材雄，人望而畏，出身事主，落落有將帥之風，見義能勇，聽受不疑，忠於事君，長於應變，誠一代之賢將也。 觀恒山之役，立談釋二帥之憾； 涇師之亂，號哭赴奉天之危，可不為忠義乎！ 對白華之進軍，知平涼之必詐，沮星變之議，移渭橋之軍，可不為應變乎！ 解帶結孝忠之心，請婚釋延賞之怨，嫉惡有楚琳之請，懲亂行希鑒之誅，可不為明於決斷乎！ 而德宗皇帝聽斷不明，無人君之量，俾功臣困讒慝之口，奸人秉衡石之權，丁瓊之言，誠堪太息。 雖齪齪刻渭橋之石，區區賜煙閣之銘，亦何心哉！ 作善遺慶，諸子俱才，元和平賊之功，聽、愬居其半。 父子昆弟，皆以功名始終，道家所忌之談，李氏以善勝矣。
The historian remarks: The Western Pacifier was grand in stature and heroic in talent; men looked on him with awe. From his first service he bore a commander's bearing — bold when justice demanded, swift to heed counsel, loyal to his sovereign, skilled in adaptation — a worthy general of his age. At Heng Mountain, a few words standing released two commanders' grievances; in the Jing army rebellion, he wept and rushed to Fengtian's peril — was this not loyal righteousness! facing Baihua's advance, he saw Pingliang must be a feint; he blocked counsel from omens and shifted the army at Wei Bridge — was this not adaptability! loosening his belt won Zhu Xiaozhong's loyalty; seeking marriage dissolved Zhang Yanshang's grudge; rejecting Chu Lin showed hatred of evil; executing Xi Jian punished rebellion — was this not decisive judgment! Yet Dezong judged poorly and lacked a ruler's breadth, letting worthy servants be trapped by slander while wicked men held power — Ding Qiong's case truly merits a sigh. Though he carved the stone at Wei Bridge and granted an inscription in the Cloud of Glory Pavilion — what was in his heart! Good deeds leave blessings; all his sons had talent. Of the Yuanhe era's merit in pacifying rebels, Ting and Su accounted for half. Father, sons, and brothers alike began and ended in merit and fame. What Daoists warn against, the Li family overcame through virtue.
45
贊曰：桓桓太師，義勇天資。 運鐘禍亂，力拯顛危。 愬事章武，誅蔡平齊。 淩煙畫圖，父子為宜。
In praise: Grand and mighty the Grand Mentor — righteous courage was his heaven-given gift. When calamity struck, he strove with all his strength to save a tottering realm. Su served Zhangwu, destroyed Cai, and pacified Qi. Painted on the Cloud-rising Terrace — father and sons were fit indeed.
